races.name: Dooley Insurance Irish EBF Fillies Maiden

runners_data.name: April Mist
runners_data.comment: Debut filly by Cotai Glory out of smart sprinter Summerseat Mist, with a half-sister useful at 7f; connections capable of producing them sharp first time and the 5f trip looks right — watch the market closely.

runners_data.name: Bettercalltheboss
runners_data.comment: Nando Parrado filly drawn wide in stall 9; a half-sister to a 6f debut scorer in France offers some encouragement, but the wide berth is a concern on debut and she is probably best assessed through the market before committing.

runners_data.name: Brazilian Diva
runners_data.comment: Speedily bred and has course and distance experience, finishing third in recent starts, but a small filly found herself outclassed in an auction race last time and needs another drop in grade to be competitive.

runners_data.name: Celestial Crown
runners_data.comment: Agonisingly close to success on debut at Cork, going down by a short head, and the winner has since taken a Listed prize — that form makes this one of the better-credentialled runners in the field; in-form yard and normal progression could see her go one better here.

runners_data.name: Hip Hop Chrissy
runners_data.comment: Showed useful early pace on debut at Listowel, finishing third, and switching back to 5f at a demanding track should suit a horse that has already handled good ground — the stable has taken this prize before and further progress is expected.

runners_data.name: Lady Patrona
runners_data.comment: Runner-up on second start before getting too enthusiastic over a longer trip at the Curragh on her latest outing; the drop back in distance plays to her strengths at 5-6f and she has done enough in recent starts that landing a maiden is within reach — the wide draw from stall 10 is the one concern.

runners_data.name: Madam Secretary
runners_data.comment: Showed real promise at Listowel on debut, beaten five lengths in third, and that form has since been given a boost; suited by 6f and a trainer with a fine record at this track who can extract further progress — worth a place at least.

runners_data.name: Red Primrose
runners_data.comment: Blackbeard filly closely related to a smart 2yo performer impressive at 6-7f; from a yard that routinely runs juveniles first time and the market will be the best guide — draw in stall 8 and a March foaling date suggest she will improve with experience.

runners_data.name: Shi Yang
runners_data.comment: Blackbeard filly who cost 55,000gns and has an unraced dam, so there is limited hard evidence to go on; the stable has a strong history with its juveniles so she merits monitoring in the market, but on breeding alone she is hard to assess.

runners_data.name: Tatianna
runners_data.comment: Back for a third start at 5f on going she handles, but failed to settle when stepped up in trip last time and got very free — she needs to relax better here, and while the trip switch back is a plus, temperament is the key question.

races.name: ARKequine Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: Billboa
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for W P Browne with a modest sim-going record of 2 placings from 15 runs; needs traffic to part and a strong gallop to close into, neither of which this race shape is likely to deliver.
runners_data.comment: Tongue-tie applied for the first time as connections look for an answer; Billboa has a wide draw and faces a stiff mark after struggling in recent starts at Dundalk and elsewhere, and while the all-weather form is stronger, today's conditions represent a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Reinforce
runners_data.note: Returning from a 356-day absence for Miss K Brown, which is a significant fitness concern; hold-up style and strong placings on good ground look appealing in theory but the layoff and pace scenario both count against a bold reappearance.
runners_data.comment: Away for nearly a year and showing a regressive profile before the layoff, finding no rhythm at Bellewstown last time; the wide draw adds difficulty, and this six-year-old needs to recapture his best to be a factor at 5f on good ground.

runners_data.name: Happy Henry
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner, with a recent form line of 3-5-2-3-3-1 showing consistent competitiveness and a win at 5f on good; Leigh Roche takes the ride and he has strong hold on the early lead, making him the pivotal horse in this race shape — marked as racing slightly out of role per style fit score, but his natural front-running profile suits perfectly here.
runners_data.comment: Got off the mark in first-time cheekpieces at Navan 17 days ago, benefiting from a strong pace and a stiff track; the cheekpieces go on again and the mark still looks manageable for a horse that may have more to offer now that he has opened his account.

runners_data.name: Tawaazon
runners_data.note: Experienced eight-year-old for J A Kinsella who has raced 14 of his last 15 starts on similar ground, giving excellent going confidence; hold-up style means he needs the field to slow and compress for him to pounce, and he faces the same late-closing problem as the rest of the overcrowded hold-up brigade.
runners_data.comment: Tawaazon has gone below his best since a break and a flat effort on easy ground at Leopardstown last time suggests he did not stay; tongue-tie fitted for the first time and dropping back in trip, he handles soft and good but has much to prove after a string of disappointing runs.

runners_data.name: Polar Bear
runners_data.note: Mrs Harrington's six-year-old whose five-run history shows a career best of 3rd at 5f on good; genuine hold-up type who needs cut in the ground and a fierce pace to be effective, and this uncontested-leader scenario offers him little.
runners_data.comment: Polar Bear holds decent form at 5-7f when the ground yields, but a blank run at Fairyhouse last time suggests the quicker surface left him flat; first-time hood fitted and the mark is fair for a horse who is better than his record suggests, though inconsistency remains the nagging doubt.

runners_data.name: Mehmar
runners_data.note: Six-year-old who has scored zero wins and zero places on similar going from 7 attempts, suggesting the surface is not ideal; Seamie Heffernan takes the ride but the hold-up style and poor going record make him a tough back.
runners_data.comment: Switched headgear again after the visor failed to spark any improvement in a claimer last time; suited by 6-7f, Mehmar has been on a long losing run and is inconsistent, though a clean run on sound footing could see him closer than recent efforts suggest.

runners_data.name: Hooves Your Daddy
runners_data.note: Three-year-old in form, placing twice at 5f recently including a 2nd and 3rd; hold-up-labelled but placed prominently enough to land a competitive spot just off the pace, and Ronan Whelan's experience in big fields is an asset — solid each-way profile if he gets a clean run.
runners_data.comment: Hooves Your Daddy shaped well for much of the season before a combination of a slow start, interference and a step up in trip conspired against him at Fairyhouse 12 days ago — back at his best distance and with that run behind him, he can get back to his best.

runners_data.name: Jazzit
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse for T G McCourt whose three 5f/6f places on better ground suggest ability; pushed into a midfield map slot because the race is over-subscribed with closers, and style fit score of 0.90 reflects that racing out of his natural rear position limits his winning chance.
runners_data.comment: Showed a range of form including a near-miss over course and distance before a flat run up in class last time; now fitted with first-time cheekpieces and back on going she handles, Jazzit has the ability to land a race at this level if she reproduces her better efforts.

runners_data.name: Sayonara
runners_data.note: Three-year-old for A Slattery with only 1 run on similar going from 5 and finishing 16th on good last time; hold-up profile and weak form makes her hard to recommend in this tactical scenario.
runners_data.comment: A consistent all-weather type who has yet to transfer that form convincingly to turf; trainer is struggling for winners right now and Sayonara failed to fire on her handicap debut at Fairyhouse last time — she remains yet to score at this level and faces a stiff ask on today's going.

runners_data.name: Ballysax Lil' Mick
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran with a win and a place at 5f on good ground; his true nature as a hold-up runner is compressed into midfield mapping due to the overcrowded rear, and the style fit score of 0.92 cautions against expecting his best effort here.
runners_data.comment: Shaped with promise back from a break at Navan last time, just tiring near the finish — experience and improvement expected from that run; at this mark over 5f on going she handles, Ballysax Lil' Mick is entitled to go closer.

runners_data.name: Hero Of The Hour
runners_data.note: Veteran nine-year-old for William Delahunty who has placed 3 times in 15 similar-going runs including a win at 6f; races with a prominent style that could genuinely challenge for position behind Happy Henry, making him one of the better-placed tactical beneficiaries in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Back from a break and just found the final furlong beyond him at Fairyhouse 12 days ago, though he was in the hunt to a degree; a first outing in a visor and dropping in at the weights in a big field, Hero Of The Hour has the profile to put things right on a track and surface that suits him.

runners_data.name: Whatswrongnow
runners_data.note: Consistent 5f/6f performer with four placings from 15 similar-going starts, all at distances matching today; prominent style suits this scenario well and recent form shows two 2nds on good ground — he is credibly placed if he secures a position just off the pace.
runners_data.comment: Found the pace elusive late in recent runs but came back to better form at Fairyhouse recently, going down narrowly off a lower mark; that tenacity in tight finishes is encouraging and Whatswrongnow arrives here in form — the wide draw from stall 19 is the main risk.

runners_data.name: Platino Bianco
runners_data.note: Five-year-old for Conor Maxwell whose best recent effort was 6th at 6f on good; a natural hold-up horse who finds himself mapped to midfield due to the crowded rear, and the style fit score of 0.92 is a genuine caution against rating his tactical chance too highly.
runners_data.comment: Lost ground without excuses at Fairyhouse last time and has failed to hit the frame in recent starts; fitted with first-time headgear in a tongue visor combination, Platino Bianco is on a lowly mark but needs to find significantly more to get involved.

runners_data.name: Snowballs
runners_data.note: Four-year-old from W McCreery's yard returning after 36 days, with a tongue tie in place and an all-7s-and-8s recent form profile; genuine hold-up type shifted to midfield by the over-supply of closers, and no winning or placing form on similar going in 9 tries.
runners_data.comment: Has found little since entering handicap company, with a string of moderate efforts and a missed break at Cork last time; Snowballs is effective at 5f and handles the ground, but the first-time visor needs to unlock something that has been absent for several runs.

runners_data.name: Whats It All About
runners_data.note: Three-year-old tagged with a finishing fade flag who has never placed on similar going from 5 runs; the redistribution into midfield merely compounds the challenge for a horse who already struggles to see out his races.
runners_data.comment: Bred to want further than 6f and has looked underpowered in recent starts; the evidence from latest runs at the Curragh points to this trip being too sharp, and while connections may try to find a niche, the profile makes it hard to be confident today.

runners_data.name: Spiced Gold
runners_data.note: Three-year-old for T G McCourt whose form reads 00-060 and who also carries a fade-in-finish flag; shifted out of the true hold-up position into midfield, and the trainer has two runners in this race which complicates stable intent slightly.
runners_data.comment: Struggling for form across recent starts and yet to show anything on going that suits; connections are searching for the right conditions but Spiced Gold has been tailed off at Fairyhouse recently and needs a lot to go right to be competitive.

runners_data.name: Steel Magnolia
runners_data.note: Four-year-old from W McCreery who placed 3 times from 14 similar-going runs, including a 3rd and 4th; hold-up by nature but mapped into midfield given the overcrowded rear — one of the more interesting outsider profiles if the race becomes a scramble.
runners_data.comment: Performed consistently at this level earlier in the season, beaten a length and a half off a mark 3lb higher at Cork last time; drawn toward the inside in stall 3 in a large field and handles cut — a touch frustrating in the maiden department but in reasonable nick and worth respect.

runners_data.name: Realtin Fantasy
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old returning from a 236-day absence with five place finishes from 15 similar-going runs but no wins; the lengthy layoff is the obvious concern and the redistribution from her natural hold-up position means she will not be racing to her strengths today.
runners_data.comment: Has been a poor traveller in recent outings and dropped away at Dundalk before a long break; back with a first-time hood after 236 days off, Realtin Fantasy handles sound surfaces and is best at 5f — all to prove here but not without an outside chance if the layoff has freshened her.

runners_data.name: Apache Star
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with a tongue tie and blinkers combination whose best recent efforts were two 6ths on similar ground; hold-up profile and modest ratings make it hard to identify a convincing route to contention in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Set overly strong fractions in recent handicap starts and came unstuck again at Fairyhouse last time; tongue-tie applied for the first time and dropping back in trip, Apache Star is effective at 5f on a range of going but needs to demonstrate she can pace her effort — form has deteriorated sharply.

runners_data.name: Bel Espoir
runners_data.note: Four-year-old carrying a fade-in-finish tag with a form line of 0-0900 and a history of finishing well back; shifted into midfield from his natural rear position, the combination of the finish-fade flag and redistribution makes him one of the least likely winners in the field.
runners_data.comment: Beaten down the field at Fairyhouse last time and has failed to produce anything of note across recent starts; effective at 6f, Bel Espoir is on the minimum mark but has given no indication in recent runs that she can change that trend today.

runners_data.name: Livingston Range
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran with two 4ths from his last two runs on good ground suggesting he is in a reasonable vein; hold-up profile and the mapping compression mean he will not be racing from his ideal spot, though his consistency at this distance is mildly interesting.
runners_data.comment: Showed a degree of consistency in recent 5f handicaps, fourth at Fairyhouse last time on a trip she handles well; drawn wide in stall 22 in a big field and on a basement mark — improving form suggests she can stay competitive, but the long losing run tempers expectations.

runners_data.name: You Smiled
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who carries a finishing-fade flag and has only three career runs, all finishing 7th, 10th, 9th; minimal experience and a fade tendency in a 24-runner field over 5f on soft-ish ground makes this a very difficult assignment.
runners_data.comment: Showed a progression on her most recent qualifying run at Cork, going closer in a maiden, and connections believe the opening handicap mark is lenient; with her sire effective at 6f and her dam smart over 7f, there is pace and staying power in the mix — the tongue-tie goes on and she could outrun her price.

runners_data.name: Another Nice'day
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a fade flag whose best recent effort was 5th at 5f on good; mapped to midfield from a natural hold-up slot, and the finishing tendency to stop late is a serious concern in a race where closers will already be at a structural disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: Largely out of form in recent handicap starts and got very free at Fairyhouse last time; effective at 5-6f but has looked moderate when asked to settle — the fresh headgear may help but Another Nice'day needs a clean bill of behavioural health to deliver.

runners_data.name: Mini Cotai
runners_data.note: Three-year-old for M Mulvany who ran just five days ago, with headgear applied and a form line showing 2nd and 4th recently at 5f on soft; quick turnaround is notable but the recent fitness is an asset — hold-up type who finds himself in midfield due to the overcrowded rear, though he has more profile than many of the redistributed horses to emerge late if the race fractures.
runners_data.comment: Back to form at Down Royal last time, going down by three-quarters of a length on soft ground, and today's conditions match; Mini Cotai handles today's going and trip well, and with a fresh set of headgear fitted, she arrives in reasonable shape — the extensive recent form just limits the element of surprise.

races.paceDynamic: Happy Henry is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 24-runner field and looks set to stride into an uncontested lead from the gates, with no credible rival likely to chase him down from the off on good to yielding ground over five furlongs at Naas. The pace he sets will be measured and sustainable rather than suicidal, meaning he dictates terms throughout and the race unfolds in a steady, strung-out fashion with minimal early pressure. Prominent and hold-up horses will be forced to cover ground from well off the pace, and the soft-enough conditions will make it harder to make up large margins late. This race shape strongly favours horses able to race prominently or just behind the leader — particularly Whatswrongnow, Hero Of The Hour, and Hooves Your Daddy — rather than true hold-up types who will find the moderate gallop set by a lone leader insufficient to manufacture the late momentum they need. The field holds significantly more genuine hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Jazzit, Whats It All About, Ballysax Lil' Mick, Platino Bianco, Snowballs, and several others are natural come-from-behind horses who will be unable to adopt their preferred positions, with Hero Of The Hour and Whatswrongnow best placed to actually secure competitive prominent berths.

scenarios.title: Happy Henry Wires Field
scenarios.trigger: If Happy Henry is allowed to stride clear unchallenged and controls tempo throughout, denying closers the strong gallop they need.
scenarios.body: If Happy Henry is allowed to stride clear unchallenged and controls tempo throughout, denying closers the strong gallop they need.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Run Through
scenarios.trigger: If Happy Henry is tracked closely by Hero Of The Hour and Whatswrongnow who hit the rising ground fresh and overhaul him inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Happy Henry is tracked closely by Hero Of The Hour and Whatswrongnow who hit the rising ground fresh and overhaul him inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Catch Flat Pace
scenarios.trigger: If the going rides slower than advertised and a genuinely steady early pace allows the better-handicapped hold-up horses to close powerfully in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If the going rides slower than advertised and a genuinely steady early pace allows the better-handicapped hold-up horses to close powerfully in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos Rules
scenarios.trigger: If Happy Henry is surprisingly challenged early, the pace fractures and the race becomes a scramble for position in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If Happy Henry is surprisingly challenged early, the pace fractures and the race becomes a scramble for position in the final two furlongs.

watchPoints.text: Happy Henry is the only horse likely to lead — watch whether Leigh Roche takes him straight to the front immediately from the gates, as any hesitation or crowding in a 24-runner field could see him trapped and unable to assert his natural advantage.

Hooves Your Daddy and Whatswrongnow are both hunting the same prominent positions just off Happy Henry; if they clash for the same ground in the first furlong, both could use valuable energy and the tactical edge they carry in this scenario evaporates.

Several redistributed hold-up horses — including Jazzit, Ballysax Lil' Mick, and Platino Bianco — will be racing in an unfamiliar midfield position; watch for traffic problems and wide-running as these horses try to find their feet in positions that do not suit their natural rhythm.

races.name: Race & Stay Irish Racing Tours Rated Race

runners_data.name: Go Just Do It
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for J P O'Brien and Dylan Browne McMonagle, last seen 32 days ago and stepping back to 6f; his 4-win-or-place record in 5 runs on similar ground is the key asset, though his most recent effort (9th) is a concern that keeps him from being a certainty despite controlling the pace.
runners_data.comment: Has a win over course and distance but could not last home over a mile in a Group 1 last time; the return to 6f at a stiff track suits and he has more to offer — the main risk is whether that top-level exposure has dulled his edge in a shorter race.

runners_data.name: Amiata
runners_data.note: Nicola Burns partners this G M Lyons three-year-old who owns course-and-distance winning form (1/6f/GOO) and arrives on a 21-day turnaround in good nick; she is genuinely a front-running/prominent type by style, mapped rearward only because the prominent berths are oversubscribed, so her actual chance is better than her shown position implies if she can secure an early forward slot.
runners_data.comment: Building form in handicaps and recently got back to landing a race at the Curragh by a neck; effective at 5-6f on a range of going and stepping up in class here — the leap from handicap company brings unknowns but the improving profile makes her a genuine factor.

runners_data.name: Gavoo
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer for D Marnane who stays genuinely in role here and has solid 6f form (1/6f/STA, 4/6f/GOO); the 32-day break and a poor last run (9th, 7f) are minor flags, but dropping back to his winning trip on a surface within his comfort zone (7/8 similar-going record) makes him a live contender tracking Go Just Do It.
runners_data.comment: Disappointing when stepped up in trip at the Curragh last time, but prior to that had been running consistently well; effective at 6f on a sound surface and the drop back in distance is a positive — needs to recapture his previous level to be competitive against good opponents.

runners_data.name: Oro Blanco
runners_data.note: Shane Foley partners this J Harrington three-year-old who has only three career runs and a win over 7f; he is a natural prominent type whose instinct will be to race up with the pace, but he has been displaced to midfield by the weight of front-runners in this field, and his short form profile over slightly longer trips makes the drop to 6f on yielding ground a mild stamina query rather than a worry.
runners_data.comment: Landed a maiden at Fairyhouse by two and a half lengths last time, travelling smoothly and putting the race to bed decisively; progressive profile and effective at 7f-1m on yielding and good — this step into better company is warranted and, with the form behind him sound, he merits favouritism.

races.paceDynamic: Go Just Do It is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only four runners and no genuine challenger to his lead, he will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset over this 6f trip on Good to Yielding ground at Naas. Gavoo is the only other horse racing genuinely in role at the prominent position, meaning Go Just Do It faces minimal pressure and can set whatever fractions suit him. Amiata and Oro Blanco are both natural prominent types who have been redistributed rearward by the mapping process — there are simply too many pace-committed horses for all to occupy their natural berth, and Go Just Do It and Gavoo are most likely to actually secure the front positions. This race shape strongly favours horses who can press or track a steady-to-moderate pace and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs, rather than those relying on a late burst off a genuinely fast early tempo that is unlikely to materialise.

scenarios.body: If Go Just Do It bowls along uncontested and sets a measured pace that suits his stamina over the 6f trip.

scenarios.body: If Gavoo disputes the lead more aggressively and puts Go Just Do It under early pressure, raising the tempo.

scenarios.title: Redistributed Prominent Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Amiata, despite being mapped rearward, manages to slot prominently early and finds the steady pace perfectly timed for her finishing effort.
scenarios.body: If Amiata, despite being mapped rearward, manages to slot prominently early and finds the steady pace perfectly timed for her finishing effort.

scenarios.title: Late Surge From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and leave a closing opportunity from off the pace.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and leave a closing opportunity from off the pace.

watchPoints.text: Go Just Do It will be closely watched in the early stages — if McMonagle allows him to stride clear unchallenged and the sectionals are modest, his control of the race becomes the single most important factor in the outcome.

Amiata's starting position and how quickly Nicola Burns sends her forward are critical: if she gets trapped behind the two natural front-runners at the break, her redistribution from true prominent to effective hold-up becomes a real tactical disadvantage.

Gavoo's willingness to press Go Just Do It rather than sit passively is the key swing factor — if he tests the leader's pace, the tempo rises and the race shape changes materially from a solo-led affair to a contested duel.

With only four runners and Ground to Yielding conditions, the pace is unlikely to be truly strong — watch for a slowly-run first 2f that compresses the field and narrows the winning margin, potentially suiting any horse that can quicken off a slow tempo rather than grind it out.

races.name: Al Shira'aa Racing Irish EBF Jannah Rose Stakes (Fillies' Group 3)

runners_data.name: Cameo
runners_data.note: Won over 12f at Leopardstown in May, handles soft ground well (4/7 on similar going), and Lordan/Aidan O'Brien partnership gives her plenty of tactical options from a prominent pitch — the key question is whether she can sustain the effort over this longer trip against higher-class rivals.
runners_data.comment: Two wins from five recent starts, including a clear-cut success before a tough assignment in Group 1 company at Epsom last time, where she was sent forward too freely on ground clearly too soft; back on quicker going which she handles well and dropping back in grade, the Epsom run can be taken with a pinch of salt — she has the class for this level.

runners_data.name: Caught U Sleeping
runners_data.note: Bounced back to win a Leopardstown 10f maiden on good ground 46 days ago and has run at or near the pace in all her starts; the break since last run is worth noting but N Meade runners often return fresh, and Ben Coen should have her tracking the leader throughout.
runners_data.comment: Landed a Listed prize here by three-quarters of a length last time, finding extra when challenged — a performance that marked a significant step forward and she could have more to offer over longer trips; the gap since that run is the only flag.

runners_data.name: Della Pace
runners_data.note: George Boughey's filly has placed twice at 10f including on soft, giving her the stamina credentials, but her natural inclination is to race prominently and with five runners of similar persuasion she will likely find herself racing in a more restrained fashion than ideal, which tempers confidence.
runners_data.comment: Moved well through races at Goodwood last time, hitting the frame once more in Listed company and edging closer to that level with each run; suited by today's trip and going and progressive — the risk is that she remains vulnerable in the highest grade.

runners_data.name: La Fogata
runners_data.note: A Donnacha O'Brien filly who has won over 8f on good ground and ran a decent second over 10f last time, but she naturally wants to race on the pace — the redistribution to hold-up here reflects a crowded prominent group rather than her own inclination, and she may well edge forward from that mapped position.
runners_data.comment: Made steady progress in handicap and Listed company but found herself asked to challenge a shade early on her latest outing over a shorter trip; effective at a mile and suited by today's distance — a positive, patient ride could see her finish strongly.

runners_data.name: Pollenca
runners_data.note: Won a 7f heat at The Curragh on heavy ground in April and step up to 10f has been adequate, but she has been quiet on good ground (0W0P in 2 similar-going starts) and, like several here, will struggle to find her natural racing position with so many prominent types in the field.
runners_data.comment: Ran respectably when fourth in a Listed race here last time over this trip, which was a better effort than she had shown before; may stay further than today's distance and there could be more improvement available, but she has a significant gap to close on form against these rivals.

runners_data.name: Rebel Moon
runners_data.note: Single start winner over 10f on soft for JP O'Brien and Dylan Browne McMonagle — class stands out with an OR of 120 in a race where next-best is 104, and her front-running role should be uncontested, though the 76-day absence is the one question mark against an otherwise dominant tactical profile.
runners_data.comment: An eye-catching debut scorer at Gowran Park, putting the field away by a length and a half in a maiden on her only start, and that form has been enhanced by a stablemate's subsequent Group-race effort; off a break, she handles soft and this step up in class is entirely warranted — she demands serious respect.

runners_data.name: Sinmara
runners_data.note: JP O'Brien's second string ridden by Declan McDonogh, with a win over 8f on soft and placed efforts at 7f; she naturally wants to be prominent and has the connections to suggest she will be ridden aggressively, giving her the best chance of the reshuffled mid-pack horses to actually reclaim a forward position.
runners_data.comment: Ran to her form in a Group 1 last time and was found out at the highest level; in good shape before that and effective at 7-8f, but today's trip requires more than she has shown so far — connections have a strong record in this race though she looks the second string.

races.paceDynamic: Rebel Moon is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with Dylan Browne McMonagle aboard for JP O'Brien, will stride straight to the front and control proceedings at a measured, sustainable gallop over this 1m2½f trip on Good to Yielding ground. Behind her, Cameo and Caught U Sleeping are the two genuine prominent horses who will push to track her closely, meaning the first three positions are effectively accounted for before the gates open. The field holds more prominent types than can realistically occupy those slots — Sinmara, Della Pace, and Pollenca all race prominently by nature but are mapped to midfield here, and of those Sinmara (Declan McDonogh, JP O'Brien) is best placed to push forward if she breaks well, while Della Pace and Pollenca are most likely to be shuffled back. La Fogata, a natural prominent type mapped to hold-up, is the most likely to be caught wide and detached at the rear. A lone, controlled front-runner dictating a steady pace on softening ground over a stamina trip favours horses who can press or track that pace and sustain their effort — the prominent-to-midfield profile holds the dominant tactical edge here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rebel Moon Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Rebel Moon leads without serious challenge and sets an even, measured gallop that lasts the trip.
scenarios.body: If Rebel Moon leads without serious challenge and sets an even, measured gallop that lasts the trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tracker Reels Her In
scenarios.trigger: If Rebel Moon's 76-day absence blunts her finishing effort and one of the tracking pair runs past her inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Rebel Moon's 76-day absence blunts her finishing effort and one of the tracking pair runs past her inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Sneaks Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is brisk enough to string the field out and a midfield runner picks through tired rivals in the straight.
scenarios.body: If the pace is brisk enough to string the field out and a midfield runner picks through tired rivals in the straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Sweeps Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the straight and a closer produces a sustained late run from off the bridle.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses in the straight and a closer produces a sustained late run from off the bridle.

watchPoints.text: Rebel Moon's 76-day absence is the single biggest risk factor in this race — if she returns short of peak fitness she could stop suddenly in the straight despite her dominant class advantage.

Sinmara (McDonogh/JP O'Brien) is mapped to midfield but may push forward aggressively at the start, potentially creating a contested early pace if she and Cameo both attempt to track Rebel Moon from the front rank.

La Fogata (Donnacha O'Brien) is shown in hold-up but will instinctively try to race prominently — watch for her making up ground on the outside early, which could compromise her energy reserves on testing ground.

The going is reported Good to Yielding across all Naas races today (described as Good to Soft in the race header) — any further softening during the card will increase the premium on stamina and proper pacemaking, favouring Rebel Moon's controlled front-running style even more strongly.

Cameo's form profile (win over 12f on good, placed over 12f on soft) makes her the most reliable stayer in the chasing group — if Rebel Moon fades she is the first horse punters should be looking to as the beneficiary.

races.name: Colm White Bookmaker Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Doctor Grace
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with recent good-ground win over 12f (1/12f/GOO) and strong sim-going record of 1W1P from 3 runs; A McGuinness yard is in form at 1/28 over 14 days and Gabriella Hill takes the ride — the 1m3f trip looks well within range and no going concern.
runners_data.comment: Has form including a clear-cut win three starts back but was well beaten off a tough mark last time; inconsistent and the trainer is under pressure for winners right now — first-time hood may help but the mark and recent form make the task difficult.

runners_data.name: Derry Lad
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old hold-up type who genuinely fades in the finish according to his flag, making this trip and pace dynamic a concern; sim-going record of 0W1P from 13 runs on similar ground is poor, and 40 days since last run adds uncertainty despite the tp headgear.
runners_data.comment: Out of form and beaten well in a handicap at Leopardstown last time; fitted with tongue-tie and blinkers for the first time, Derry Lad is effective at 10-12f but has been declining and needs a significant turnaround to feature over 11f here.

runners_data.name: Dancing Steve
runners_data.note: Long-absentee returning after 271 days off, and a visor is fitted — the last run showed a 13th of 13 in similar conditions, and though he won over 10f on good ground, the comeback angle and weak sim-going record (1W2P from 8) make him hard to rely on.
runners_data.comment: Away for nine months and was below his best before the layoff, beaten well at Dundalk; effective over 9-12f on good ground and the all-weather, but the long absence and out-of-form trainer are substantial hurdles — the first-time visor adds interest but there is much to prove.

runners_data.name: Glendower
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse by style with an unbeaten sim-going record for places (0W5P from 11) suggesting consistency without winning; most recent form includes a 3rd over 10f at Naas but he has struggled in bigger fields over longer trips — trainer Doyle has been quiet at 0/7 in the past 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Set too strong a pace at Limerick last time and paid the price; first-time tongue-tie fitted and handles today's going and distance — the mark is lenient relative to earlier form but a temperamental liability who needs to settle to show his best.

runners_data.name: Killyclogher Rose
runners_data.note: Style unknown (U flag) and the lightest recent form record of the field with only three starts, all on standard going; 166 days since last run and no headgear — complete unknown quantity who may need the experience in a field this large.
runners_data.comment: Flashed ability in maiden company over further before finding the drop in trip left her outpaced at Dundalk; effective at 12f on the all-weather and making her handicap debut — likely to benefit from this experience but will need the trip and probably further in time.

runners_data.name: Casheldale Lass
runners_data.note: Prominent type with two wins at 10f on good ground and a decent sim-going record of 2W3P from 8; trainer Kinirons is quiet at T14:0/2 but the horse placed last time out and the step to 11f (1m3f) from her usual 10f trips is a question worth monitoring — McGettigan's claim could help the weight.
runners_data.comment: Inconsistent record and well beaten at Fairyhouse last time with nothing to point to in mitigation; effective over 10-11f on heavy and good, first-time hood fitted — has the ability on a good day but the form figures going in are hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Ohmali
runners_data.note: Has run prominently and placed at 8f and 10f on good ground, but the step to 1m3f from a career high of 10f is a genuine stamina query; sim-going record of 0W1P from 10 on similar conditions is modest, and trainer Lupini is quiet at T14:0/6.
runners_data.comment: Got involved too early and went too fast at Limerick last time, but was a genuine threat on the run before that; effective at 7-10f on heavy and good, and if handled more patiently here Ohmali can bounce back — inconsistency is the concern.

runners_data.name: Elusive Duke
runners_data.note: Placed in six of his last eight starts and second over 10f on good ground recently — a consistent prominent type whose sim-going record (1W4P from 12) shows he handles these conditions well; the 1m3f is the longest he has run, which is worth watching, but the profile suits a race of this shape.
runners_data.comment: Went very close at Gowran Park last time, beaten a short head after a drop in class — that form places him right in the mix and connections will be encouraged; effective on a sound surface at 8-10f, and with the latest effort standing up well, he can go one better here if conditions remain fair.

runners_data.name: Forlio
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type — his natural style is to race off the pace over longer trips — but with so many closers in the field he is unlikely to get the deep cover he ideally wants; form over 16-19f trips on good ground shows a win and two places, and trainer Flynn is in form at T14:2/16, but the redistribution to midfield means he is racing out of his most effective role here.
runners_data.comment: Came on for hurdle experience and shaped with a degree of promise at Punchestown most recently; effective at 10-11f on the Flat but has never finished in the money at a mark this elevated — the switch back to Flat company is interesting and he will improve, but it may come just a run too soon.

runners_data.name: Anchors Away
runners_data.note: Carries a "fades in finish" flag and a style-fit discount having been pushed out of his natural hold-up position into midfield; his best recent run was a 4th over 10f on good ground, and while the sim-going record (0W0P from 4) on similar conditions is bare, the 27-day freshener is neutral — Quinn has had no starters in the past 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Came back from a break in reasonable shape at Fairyhouse, finishing fourth, but consistency has been an issue and the form is modest; first-time tongue-tie fitted and handles good ground and the all-weather over 10-11f — the latest run will have done her good but there is more to prove.

runners_data.name: Rising Sky
runners_data.note: Has a win over 10f on standard going and is placed in sim-going conditions once from 7, but the 0W1P record on similar ground is thin; a prominent runner who wants to be handy — the large field could cause traffic issues early but the tb headgear suggests he can travel well.
runners_data.comment: Got off the mark at Dundalk three starts back before two poor efforts since; all-weather form is stronger than the turf record and the latest run — where she missed the start — looks an anomaly worth dismissing; effective at 7-11f and 2lb lower here, a bounce back is needed but she has a profile to do so.

runners_data.name: Oust
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner and highest-rated horse in the field at OR 72, giving him a class edge on paper — he will set the fractions unchallenged, which is a significant tactical advantage; a style-fit flag notes he may not be a natural front-runner at this trip (career best trips are shorter), so his ability to see out 1m3f on Good to Yielding is the key uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Pulled a little hard at Down Royal last time but still finished a clear second, beaten six lengths; the form has since been given a boost and Oust handles 10f well on yielding going — further progress in handicaps at this trip looks likely, with the distance an important positive.

runners_data.name: I'm Flattered
runners_data.note: Returning after a huge 622-day absence (19 jockey bookings suggest this is a comeback run) and her form over 16-20f trips is on much longer distances than this 1m3f test; placed once at Goodwood, but the combination of long absence, shorter-than-ideal trip and redistribution out of hold-up position makes her a speculative runner at best.
runners_data.comment: Generally consistent over hurdles but has shown nothing on the Flat across three starts; fitted with tongue-tie first time and the hurdling fitness may help, though the level of improvement needed to compete here is very substantial.

runners_data.name: Amrum
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on good ground 23 days ago for the powerful G M Lyons yard, with a sim-going record of 1W1P from 4; clocked in at the lowest weight in the field (121lbs) with Nicola Burns claiming — the step up to 1m3f should suit a horse who has been winning prominently and finishing with purpose, and Lyons is in form at T14:1/9.
runners_data.comment: Scraped home by a head at Gowran Park last time, landing a handicap off a 7lb lower mark in a determined finish; from top connections and bred to stay further than today's trip — cheekpieces added and with the mark likely still ahead of where the assessor has him, he can follow up.

runners_data.name: Neon Eyes
runners_data.note: Has placed twice at 10f on good ground and is trained by the in-form Cromwell yard (T14:9/53 — the standout trainer record in this field); the step from 8-10f to 1m3f is a genuine trip query, and the h headgear is noted, but the prominent style and trainer form make him hard to ignore despite the distance doubt.
runners_data.comment: Went close at Gowran Park last time, finishing a head down after the pace collapsed late, and that run was the best in recent starts; bred for middle distances and handles today's ground well — still early in the handicap journey but the trajectory is upward and the mark is reasonable.

runners_data.name: Priorstown
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 3-year-old from the powerful Murtagh yard (T14:6/35), with only three career starts and best run a 6th of 8 at Heathrow; the 47-day gap and bare sim-going record (0W0P from 2) give little to work with, but the trainer's strike rate suggests he could be quietly well-prepared for this step up to 1m3f.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in a maiden on his most recent start and needing more now he faces the handicapper; from a good stable and an in-form trainer, with enough stamina in the pedigree to get further — probably still finding his feet but the current mark is a challenge.

runners_data.name: Jazz Forever
runners_data.note: Carries a "fades in finish" flag and has been redistributed from his natural hold-up position — his form is over 13-17f trips, making this 1m3f potentially short of his ideal; Reserve 1 jockey booking adds uncertainty, and the Flynn yard already has Forlio in the race, so stable preference is unclear.
runners_data.comment: Came close at Navan last time on his Flat return, going down by half a length off a slightly lower mark; effective at 10-13f on yielding and the all-weather, and the form is not easy to build on given the cold trainer stats — a horse that can run well but reliability is the question.

runners_data.name: Cameclose
runners_data.note: Showed a placed effort at 10f on good ground (2nd) but has since run poorly, and the "fades in finish" flag combined with a 2-day turnaround since last run (extremely quick return) is a significant concern; Reserve 2 jockey booking adds further uncertainty, and the redistribution away from hold-up position means he is unlikely to race in his most comfortable role.
runners_data.comment: Back to form at Ballinrobe last time, finishing second in a claimer — a step back from maidens to a claimer is noted; generally consistent and effective at 7-11f, though the quick turnaround and the switch back to handicap company add uncertainty — the first-time blinkers are the hook.

races.paceDynamic: Oust is the confirmed front-runner and, in a field of 18 over 1m3f on Good to Yielding ground at Naas, will look to dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable gallop — there is no identified rival to press or challenge him for the lead, so he can set his own rhythm. The prominent contingent of Doctor Grace, Casheldale Lass, Ohmali, Elusive Duke, Rising Sky and Neon Eyes will jostle for position behind him, meaning the early-to-middle portions of the race are unlikely to be truly dawdling but equally unlikely to be a true test of stamina. Several horses flagged as genuine hold-up types — Forlio, Anchors Away, Jazz Forever, Cameclose and I'm Flattered — have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the field holds more true closers than the rear of the race can naturally accommodate; of these, Forlio and Anchors Away are perhaps most capable of securing a genuine midfield berth given their profile, but none should be expected to get the deep late-race cover they ideally want. The race shape strongly favours horses who can track an uncontested pace from a prominent or close-midfield position and produce a sustained finish in the straight, rather than those requiring a true fast-run race to deliver a late burst from off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Oust Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Oust sets a measured, uncontested gallop and the pace is steady enough to leave a sprint finish from the front two or three furlongs out.
scenarios.body: If Oust sets a measured, uncontested gallop and the pace is steady enough to leave a sprint finish from the front two or three furlongs out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Steady Gallop, Midfield Sweepers
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely modest and a pocket of closers tracking in true midfield — not the redistributed hold-up types — manage to improve smoothly from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: If the early pace is genuinely modest and a pocket of closers tracking in true midfield — not the redistributed hold-up types — manage to improve smoothly from the two-furlong pole.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Frantic Early Scramble, Closers Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If the large 18-runner field produces a scrappy, faster-than-expected early gallop as multiple prominent types compete for position behind Oust.
scenarios.body: If the large 18-runner field produces a scrappy, faster-than-expected early gallop as multiple prominent types compete for position behind Oust.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Oust Leads, Sustains All The Way
scenarios.trigger: If Oust's uncontested lead allows him to conserve enough energy to simply outstay rivals in the straight at this longer 1m3f trip.
scenarios.body: If Oust's uncontested lead allows him to conserve enough energy to simply outstay rivals in the straight at this longer 1m3f trip.

watchPoints.text: Oust's uncontested lead in a field of 18 is the defining tactical factor — watch whether he steals an advantage in the straight before rivals can organise a challenge, as the combination of no front-running rival and an 18-horse field means those nearest him at the top of the straight are best placed.

Cameclose ran just 2 days ago and carries a "fades in finish" flag — monitor closely in the betting and early market moves, as a horse this fresh from a run in a handicap of this size is worth treating with caution in your assessment.

runners_data.name: Akissfromarose
runners_data.comment: Struggled in recent maiden starts and was well beaten at the Curragh last time; blinkers fitted and a probable preference for a mile suggests today's trip may be on the sharp side — needs to show significantly more to get involved here.

runners_data.name: Cello Sonata
runners_data.comment: Debut colt by Sergei Prokofiev, a high-class sprinter, out of smart sprinter Rose Marmara, and a half-brother to a smart 5f performer; the stable is adept at preparing first-timers and the pedigree offers pace — worth monitoring in the market before final decisions are made.

runners_data.name: Chloe's Boy
runners_data.comment: Gelding whose dam was a Listed winner over 12f with a half-brother useful at 7f as a juvenile — an interesting mix of speed and staying blood; debut performance is an unknown quantity and the market will be the most reliable indicator.

runners_data.name: Coolshine
runners_data.comment: Showed minor encouragement on his only start at Limerick, tracking the leaders before fading; sired by a sprinter out of a middle-distance mare, which clouds the picture on trip — time is still on his side and another run or two will be needed to fulfil any potential.

runners_data.name: Dark Leader
runners_data.comment: Shaped with ability when placed on debut before being a bit free when beaten six lengths at Killarney last time — if he can switch off better, there is clear improvement to come; effective at 7-8f on yielding and good, with an in-form trainer, and that debut form makes him a genuine contender.

runners_data.name: Highwayman
runners_data.comment: Failed to get into contention in three starts to date, the latest at Limerick where he tracked the pace but found nothing when it mattered; bred for a mile-plus and currently on a tightening profile — needs a significant step up to compete here.

runners_data.name: I Got To Go
runners_data.comment: Half-brother to a useful 7f juvenile out of an unraced dam; from a family with some pace credentials — debut performance entirely unknown and the prudent approach is to let the market do the talking before committing.

runners_data.name: Kalir
runners_data.comment: Travelled well but was unable to find more when pressure came in first-time cheekpieces at Gowran Park, finishing a respectable fourth; effective at 8-9f on a range of going, well connected and with a break behind him — cheekpieces stay on and he is capable of improvement.

runners_data.name: Kingcharles
runners_data.comment: Below par in his two starts including a well-beaten effort at Gowran Park last time; needs a longer trip to show his best and the current distance looks sharp — connections searching for conditions that suit.

runners_data.name: Krasimir
runners_data.comment: Consistently placed across five starts, going third in a Leopardstown 3yo race six days ago with the form around him working out at Group level — blinkers applied for the first time and a step to a mile should unlock more; the highest rated in the field and the one they all have to beat.

runners_data.name: Listentodwindblow
runners_data.comment: Back to form at Gowran Park last time, finishing second beaten two lengths on soft ground — a run that showed he belongs in this grade; effective at 7-10f with cut and the form is solid — this looks an ideal opportunity to break the maiden tag.

runners_data.name: Niobite
runners_data.comment: Sprint bred and found the trip too far in two outings, the latest at the Curragh; has all to prove at today's distance and the profile suggests a furlong or two shorter might suit better — not easy to back here.

runners_data.name: Nthea Spirit
runners_data.comment: Debut gelding out of a moderate sprinting dam — not a pedigree that shouts about today's trip; likely to need this experience and the opening run may come and go without fanfare.

runners_data.name: Pinoroyale
runners_data.comment: A Pinatubo gelding who cost 75,000 euros and is a half-brother to a smart stayer; from a stable that has a strong record with debut runners in both codes — the market will reveal whether connections have something more promising beneath the surface and this is worth watching.

runners_data.name: Saliba
runners_data.comment: Showed some inexperience but still hit the frame at Gowran Park on debut, beaten six and a quarter lengths in third; that form looks solid and he has had time to mature since — handles today's trip and going, and further progress after that educational debut outing makes him a genuine threat.

runners_data.name: Transcript
runners_data.comment: Dam was a top-class 12f performer and a classic winner, while the sire adds pace; tongue-tie fitted on debut and connections regard this one as a type who can progress — an intriguing mix of stamina and speed in the pedigree.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden

runners_data.name: Hope N Pray
runners_data.comment: Unplaced in three outings and yet to find a level that suits; wide drawn in stall 2 on a big card and with nothing productive in the form book, Hope N Pray has a lot to find to be competitive here.

runners_data.name: Beatific
runners_data.comment: Twice placed over this trip at Leopardstown, shaped with enough encouragement to suggest she belongs in maiden company — bred to be suited beyond a mile and in time that stamina will come into play; tongue-tie applied first time and the form around her should come good.

runners_data.name: Capall Cuain
runners_data.comment: Flat at Fairyhouse on her only start where she showed nothing; the yard has yet to get a winner on the board and that is a concern — not much to go on at this stage.

runners_data.name: Chosen One
runners_data.comment: Came back from a break to show a degree of form at Naas, though held comfortably; bred for around 10f and more time will be needed before she fulfils her potential — a green youngster still finding her feet and probably one for handicaps later.

runners_data.name: Elmakaya
runners_data.comment: Went very close here on her latest outing, beaten a head in a maiden at Naas — debut form around her has been given a boost at Group level and she has since been fitted with cheekpieces; effective at a mile on good and should go one better here with that experience behind her.

runners_data.name: Into Tomorrow
runners_data.comment: Fell below her debut level on a return to the track, well beaten at Leopardstown; effective at 7f with cut and there is room to improve but she probably needs to settle and find her rhythm — debut promise means she is not without hope.

runners_data.name: Lecale Breeze
runners_data.comment: Showed little in a maiden at Leopardstown on her only start, never getting into the race; speed in the pedigree but a longer trip may not be the obvious solution — early days and she is likely to take time to find her range.

runners_data.name: Little Wing
runners_data.comment: Well held in her only outing at Gowran Park but the middle-distance pedigree strongly suggests she will be better suited by further trips later in her career — this experience will be educational and an improvement is possible but perhaps not enough to contend today.

runners_data.name: Misneach Sile
runners_data.comment: Debut filly by Circus Maximus whose dam was a useful 6f juvenile and with a useful half-sister at 6f — pace on both sides; the stable is in good form and the opening experience will matter, though she may need the run to fulfil potential.

runners_data.name: Moonlit Sun
runners_data.comment: Had to switch and find a gap when third on debut here — a run that has been strengthened emphatically by those behind her at both maiden and Group level; bred to stay a mile and a half and effective at a mile on good going — that debut form alone makes her the pick of these and she should be hard to beat.

runners_data.name: Nando Lily
runners_data.comment: Beaten in three maiden starts and returned after a break to be well held at the Curragh — stamina in the dam's side and the trip may suit her better than shorter, but she needs time to mature and the current profile is weak.

runners_data.name: Orphanina
runners_data.comment: Debut filly by Soldier's Call out of a dam who was useful at 8f and landed a maiden on her first outing; half-sister to a fair 8f performer — the market will signal connections' confidence and that is the most reliable guide here.

runners_data.name: Shanala
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Leopardstown in an auction race last time and has shown consistent form across two starts; effective at 9-10f on good to yielding, with cheekpieces fitted, and an in-form trainer — can run another solid race.

runners_data.name: Siesta Senorita
runners_data.comment: Showed a little on debut at Leopardstown but was held throughout; bred to be suited by a mile-plus and longer trips should unlock improvement — today's distance may still be a shade short and she probably needs a run or two to find her level.

runners_data.name: Socratea
runners_data.comment: Debut filly by Study Of Man out of a dam who was fair at 7f at two and placed over middle-to-staying distances later; the stable is adept at getting newcomers ready and the market will be watched keenly — potential trip requirements suggest this will not be the last we see of her.

runners_data.name: Sunatia
runners_data.comment: Night Of Thunder filly out of a very smart 10f mare; a half-sister to a high-class 12f performer and this stable has taken this race before — that is not a stable that enters second strings without purpose; the wide stall tempers enthusiasm but she deserves close attention.

runners_data.name: Tickle The Cat
runners_data.comment: Below the standard required in both outings, the latest at Gowran Park where she was well beaten; bred to appreciate middle distances in time but major improvement is needed before she can feature here.

runners_data.name: Vishaya
runners_data.comment: Placed twice in recent starts, including a two-length third at Dundalk, and has had a break since — the form was on an upward curve before the layoff; effective at a mile with stamina on the dam's side, and returning fresh she can be competitive again.

runners_data.name: Wearing Stars
runners_data.comment: Hit the frame at Down Royal last time, going second beaten three and a half lengths after stepping up in trip — a trainer in excellent form and the tongue-tie added could help; effective at 6-7f on a range of going and there looks to be a race in her from this mark.

runners_data.name: White Sand Beach
runners_data.comment: A trainer with an excellent record at this venue who has been trying this filly over longer distances in Listed company; she raced too prominently at Navan last time but back in maiden grade she has plenty on her rivals on ratings — if settled, she takes considerable beating here.
